next_round_constraints: Keep proposals focused on a small neighborhood around the best-performing families: SEIRS (fractional) with delayed_I and SEIHR with H-only; avoid broad template jumps this round.
Constrain delay_weeks search to a tight band around the apparent sweet spot (centered near 2 weeks): test {1,2,3} only, and prioritize 2 with minor variants rather than exploring larger delays.
Avoid composite observation maps (e.g., I+H) for this series in the next round unless paired with an explicit identifiability constraint; prioritize single-compartment observation (delayed_I or H).
Limit added complexity: do not introduce additional compartments beyond SEIHR or additional observation mixtures; prefer one change at a time (delay OR structure OR fractional, not multiple).
Prioritize configurations expected to improve rolling robustness (lower split-to-split sensitivity) over those that only improve a single validation window.
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity within the same SEIRS+fractional+delayed_I family: performance varies notably across delay_weeks (1 vs 2 vs 3), suggesting the fit is brittle to assumed reporting/clinical lag.

Rolling-only results indicate stability issues for some candidates (higher rolling variability and/or penalties), implying parameter/fit sensitivity across splits rather than a consistently robust shape match.

SEIHR with direct H observation is competitive on point metrics but appears to trade off against added structure/penalties; the benefit of explicit hospitalization compartment is not consistently realized across rolling splits.

Observation mapping that mixes compartments (I+H) shows degraded rolling behavior, consistent with identifiability/over-attribution between latent incidence and hospitalization states for this series.
Given high peakiness and high rate scale, some templates likely mis-time the peak (phase error) rather than purely mis-scale it, as suggested by strong dependence on delay choice.
feedback.proposer_instruction: For the next round, propose a small set of refinements centered on (A) SEIRS with fractional dynamics and delayed_I observation, primarily tuning delay_weeks in {1,2,3} with emphasis on 2, and (B) SEIHR with H-only observation as a comparator. Do not propose I+H (or other mixed) observation maps. Keep complexity minimal and vary only one modeling choice per proposal (e.g., delay only, or structure only) to diagnose whether remaining error is mainly phase (lag) vs shape (hospitalization compartment) vs fractional-memory effects. Aim for candidates that are less sensitive across rolling splits rather than narrowly optimized to a single validation segment.
